name: Alma TED

lead: Alma TED (TransEpidermal Delivery) is an in-clinic system from Alma that uses low-frequency ultrasound to make the scalp's outer barrier temporarily more permeable so a topical serum can reach the skin without needles. It is offered to people who want thicker-looking hair.

A manufacturer-associated white paper of 33 participants reported relative hair density increases of about 23% at first follow-up and 31% at six months, with no treatment-related adverse events. The study was small, open-label and uncontrolled.

paras: Treatment is done in a clinic in a series of sessions; the study used three monthly treatments, with maintenance suggested every three to six months by the manufacturer-associated report. No needles are involved.

No treatment-related adverse events were reported in the white paper. The American Hair Loss Association does not currently recommend TED as an established treatment and says FDA clearance of Alma TED+ (a 650 nm laser system) does not validate the original ultrasound system.

angle.text: People use TED sessions to try to increase hair density without injections. A small uncontrolled white paper reported density gains, and independent controlled trials have not been described.

lead: Alma TED is a hair restoration system that uses acoustic energy, including low-frequency ultrasound, to temporarily increase the permeability of the scalp's outer skin so topical preparations can reach superficial tissue without needles or incisions.[1]

People use it to try to thicken thinning hair non-surgically. Alma TED+, a later system, uses 650 nm low-level laser light and received FDA 510(k) clearance for specified hair growth indications in June 2026, based on equivalence to a previously cleared laser device.[1]
The American Hair Loss Association calls the original system a delivery technology rather than a proven regrowth treatment and says it is worth further research.[1]
infobox: TED+ (650 nm laser) cleared by FDA June 2026; original TED not[1]

paras: The concept of delivering topical ingredients through skin made temporarily more permeable by ultrasound is the basis of the system.[1] Statements about operating frequency and serum formulation come from the manufacturer and clinics rather than independent trials.

Clinic pages disagree on classification. The American Hair Loss Association states that the cleared product is TED+, a 650 nm low-level laser system, and that its clearance is not validation of the original ultrasound system or its serums.[1]

A manufacturer-associated two-center white paper enrolled 33 participants (30 women, 3 men), 31 of whom completed follow-up. It reported hair density increases of about 23% at first follow-up and 31% at six months, terminal hair count increases of about 13% and 23%, and no treatment-related adverse events.[1] The study was open-label with no control group, and only two men completed it.[1] The same page cites a 2026 Dermatologic Surgery publication and states that more independent controlled studies are needed.[1]

timeline.event: Alma TED+ (650 nm laser) receives FDA 510(k) clearance for specified hair growth indications.[1]
